title: ‘EU plan for cloud and AI falls short on digital autonomy’
content:
The EU’s proposed Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) is intended to strengthen Europe’s cloud and AI sectors and reduce its dependence on providers from outside Europe. But according to researchers at the Institute for Information Law (IViR) at the University of Amsterdam, the proposal falls short of its goal. They are also concerned about the rapid expansion of data centres and the limited attention paid to sustainability and social impact.

title: Introducing new visiting researcher: Yanjie Hu
content:
IViR is pleased to introduce our new visiting researcher Yanjie Hu. Yanjie is a third-year PhD candidate in Intellectual Property Law from China, based at the Xiamen University Intellectual Property Institute. He will conduct research at IViR for 6 months to 1 year. His doctoral project explores the legitimacy of neighbouring rights, and his research spans intellectual property law (copyright and trademark law in particular) and personality rights law.

title: Introducing…Marie-Therese Sekwenz
content:
Marie-Therese Sekwenz is a postdoctoral researcher at IViR. She works with João Pedro Quintais on the NWO Vidi project Generative AI Content Moderation: Regulation for Fundamental Rights, which examines how EU law can address the moderation of generative AI content while protecting fundamental rights, particularly freedom of expression.
